researched_by: Yorkshire Water's own recreation pages, its on-site parking schedule PDF, its recreation strategy, plus Calderdale tourism pages and BBC coverage of the Langsett charging application
policy_summary:
The opposite of Northumbrian Water, and the contrast is the finding. Northumbrian sells overnight parking at seven reservoirs on one shared booking system. Yorkshire Water sells none, anywhere, and says so in one sentence on its own parking FAQ: 'No, the car parks will not be available for overnight parking.' Thirty car parks, roughly 700 spaces, 28,000 hectares of land, and not a single pitch, bay or campsite on any of it.

So the landowner tier is not one model. It is per company after all, but the answer each company gives is different, and Yorkshire Water's answer is no.

What there is instead is a charging trial. Four car parks in the Washburn Valley - Swinsty Stack Point, Swinsty Moor, Fewston Blubberhouses and Thruscross - went to GBP1 an hour rising to GBP5 all day, with a GBP30 annual permit, ANPR cameras and payment by machine, RingGo or permit. Everywhere else is still free. The company tried to extend charging to Langsett in 2022: the Peak District National Park Authority approved it, Barnsley Council refused the same thing at Flouch, hundreds signed a petition, and the reservoir page still advertises free parking in 2026. That stalemate is the direction of travel - charging by attrition, one planning application at a time, with no provision offered in return.

The practical trap is different from the Kielder trap. At Kielder the day ticket reads like permission. Here the car parks are mostly unbarriered, unlit, free and empty after dark, which reads like permission all by itself. Only two of the thirty are physically locked at night (Baitings Embankment and Rivelin, both 'by local agreement'), and only Scammonden publishes real opening hours. Everywhere else the gate stays open and the rule is a sentence on a webpage. Height barriers are the thing that actually stops a van: the company's own schedule lists fourteen car parks with a barrier against seventeen without, and the barriered ones include every charged car park in the Washburn Valley and Thruscross at 1.8 metres.
notes:
Yorkshire Water's estate sits inside three national parks' worth of other people's rules and the layers matter. Langsett is inside the Peak District National Park but the car park is Yorkshire Water's, so the Authority's byelaw 4 (no vehicle left between midnight and 6am, GBP500 fine, prosecuted in the magistrates) does NOT apply there - it binds Authority land only. A van user at Langsett is subject to a landowner's webpage, not a byelaw, and the difference is the difference between being asked to leave and being summonsed. The same distinction runs the other way at Ogden, where Yorkshire Water owns the water and Calderdale Council runs the country park and takes the GBP1.

The recreation strategy is worth reading for what it does not say. It counts the car parks and sets an ambition to be 'a recognised leader in the recreational use of land and waters', talks about removing barriers and reaching under-represented groups, and never once mentions camping, caravans, motorhomes or staying the night. Overnight provision is not something Yorkshire Water has decided against; it appears never to have been on the table.

Enforcement reality: ANPR at the four charged car parks, rangers funded partly by the charges, and nothing but signage everywhere else. The visitor safety page confirms byelaws exist and are prosecutable, but cites them only for swimming.
open_questions: What do the Yorkshire Water reservoir byelaws actually prohibit? The PDF at /media/aqkjtded/ would not yield text through two extraction attempts. The visitor safety page confirms byelaws exist and that breaching them is an offence, but quotes them only on swimming. Whether camping or overnight vehicle use is caught is UNRESOLVED - and it decides whether the overnight rule here is a webpage or a criminal offence.

Do the four charged Washburn Valley car parks have gates, and are they locked? The parking FAQ says overnight parking is not available but publishes no closing time, and the on-site parking schedule gives hours only for Scammonden and Tophill Low.

Is Langsett Barn still free in 2026? The Peak District National Park Authority approved charging in 2022 and Barnsley refused it at Flouch; the reservoir page still says free parking. Confirm on site.

Ogden Water gate times. Calderdale Council manages the car park and takes the GBP1; the council's own page could not be retrieved. A country park car park with a visitor centre is very likely locked at dusk, but that is inference, not a source.
Exact locations of Baitings Embankment and Rivelin car parks, the only two recorded as locked at night. No postcode published for either.

sites.name: All Yorkshire Water car parks
sites.notes: The company-wide rule, stated once and plainly on the reservoir parking charges FAQ: 'No, the car parks will not be available for overnight parking.' It is framed as an answer about the four charged Washburn Valley car parks but the company publishes no contrary position anywhere else, offers no overnight facility on any of its thirty car parks, and lists no camping, caravan or bunkhouse accommodation on its whole 28,000-hectare estate. Recorded as landowner policy because that is what it is - a condition of entry, enforceable by being asked to leave, not by penalty or prosecution. Whether the reservoir byelaws add a criminal layer is unresolved; see open questions.

sites.name: Swinsty Stack Point car park
sites.price_note: GBP1 one hour, GBP2 two hours, GBP3 six hours, GBP5 all day. GBP30 annual permit; free annual permit for Blue Badge holders, who must apply in advance and are NOT automatically exempt because the cameras cannot see a badge.
sites.search_hint: Stack Point car park, Swinsty Reservoir, Washburn Valley
sites.notes: One of the four car parks in the charging trial, on the eastern edge of Swinsty. 2.2m height barrier - most panel-van conversions will not enter, and nothing taller will. Charges are payable by machine (card only), the RingGo app or an online permit, and can be settled any time up to midnight on the day of the visit. Anglers park free on the strength of their fishing ticket.

sites.name: Langsett Barn car park
sites.price_note: Free at the time of research, despite the Peak District National Park Authority approving Yorkshire Water's charging application in 2022.
sites.search_hint: Langsett Barn car park, A616, Langsett, Sheffield
sites.notes:
THE ONE TO GET RIGHT IN THIS FILE. Free, 62 spaces, no height barrier, no gate, no machine, moorland on three sides and a pub and cafe on the fourth. Everything about it says stay, and the company says no overnight parking. The second Langsett car park, Langsett Flouch, is 250 metres before the Flouch roundabout further west on the A616, has 24 spaces and DOES have a height barrier.

The legal layer is the interesting part. Langsett is inside the Peak District National Park, and the Authority's byelaw 4 makes leaving any vehicle on its land between midnight and 6am an offence carrying a GBP500 fine. That byelaw binds Authority land. This car park is Yorkshire Water's, so it does not apply here - the only rule is the landowner's, enforceable by being asked to leave. Do not read the Peak District file across onto this pin.

Charging history: Yorkshire Water applied in 2022 to charge here, the Authority approved it against a petition and local objection, and Barnsley Council refused the equivalent at Flouch. The page still says free in 2026.
sites.geocode_precision: postcode centroid for Yorkshire Water's published postcode for the car park; the car park itself is off the A616 at the north-east corner of the reservoir, so the pin sits about a kilometre north of the tarmac

sites.name: Digley Reservoir car parks (Quarry and South)
sites.notes: Two free car parks sharing 39 spaces between them - Digley Quarry at the north end (HD9 2QD) and Digley South at the southern end of the embankment (HD9 2RX). Neither has a height barrier and neither has a gate, which makes this the most van-accessible free site on the Yorkshire Water estate and therefore the one most likely to be used overnight in defiance of the policy. Above Holmfirth, in the Peak District National Park but on Yorkshire Water land, so the Authority's midnight-to-6am byelaw does not reach it.
sites.geocode_precision: postcode centroid for Digley Quarry car park, the northern of the two; the record covers both

sites.name: Scammonden Wood Edge car park
sites.search_hint: Wood Edge car park, Scammonden Water, Rishworth
sites.notes:
The only Yorkshire Water car park with published opening hours, and therefore the only one where the overnight restriction is a closure rather than a policy. The company's on-site parking schedule records it as 'car park open 09:00-18:00'. Recorded as instrument opening_hours on the Eryri precedent - shortening the hours is a different legal act from banning sleeping, and time_from/time_to here describe the shut window, not a tariff.

91 spaces, free, overlooking the M62, with a height barrier at the entrance. The other two Scammonden car parks are New Lane (14 spaces) and Sledge Gate (18), neither barriered; a third, Crull Moor, keeps the same 09:00-18:00 hours and closes entirely from November to March. Yorkshire Water's own advice is to 'check closing times detailed on site prior to setting off on your walk', which is a warning that the signs, not the website, are authoritative.
sites.geocode_precision: postcode centroid for the car park's published postcode off Low Platt Lane

sites.name: Ogden Water car park
sites.price_note: GBP1 parking charge, collected by Calderdale Council.
sites.search_hint: Ogden Water Country Park car park, Ogden Lane, Halifax
sites.notes:
Split responsibility, which is why it is easy to get wrong. Yorkshire Water owns the reservoir and lists it among its recreation sites; Calderdale Council runs Ogden Water Country Park around it, staffs the visitor centre, maintains the toilets and takes the GBP1 for the car park. Two bodies, one car park, and the answer to 'whose rule is it' is probably the council's rather than the water company's.

A country park car park with a visitor centre and a staffed gatehouse is the sort that is locked at dusk, and one directory gives site hours of 08:30-17:00 daily, but no closing time could be confirmed from Calderdale itself - the council page would not load. Treat as gated until checked. The Yorkshire Water no-overnight-parking policy applies to the land either way.
sites.geocode_precision: postcode centroid for the car park's published postcode, accessed from Ogden Lane off the A629

sites.name: Baitings Embankment and Rivelin car parks - locked at night
sites.notes:
The only two car parks on the whole Yorkshire Water estate that are physically shut at night. The company's on-site parking schedule carries the identical note against each: 'car park locked by local agreement at night'. No time is given and no agreement is named, which suggests a neighbour or a parish rather than a company policy - and means the hour will be local knowledge, not published.

Worth recording because it is the practical difference between a rule and a locked gate. Baitings is above Ripponden in Calderdale on the A58; Rivelin is in the Rivelin Valley on the Sheffield side. Both are free and both have height barriers. No postcode is published for either, so no pin.
